slides.title:
The 3 C's: Clarity 
Be Specific!
content: AI doesn't read your mind; Vague prompts give generic answers
Weak: "Write about electric cars."
Good: "Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
narration: First, let's talk about Clarity. Always be specific!
AI can't read your mind, can it?
Vague prompts will only get you generic answers.
For example, "Write about electric cars" is weak.
A good prompt, however, is specific and direct.
slides.image_prompt: Split screen: Left shows a person whispering vaguely, right shows a person pointing clearly at a specific item, with a confused AI robot on the left and an understanding one on the right.

slides.title:
The 3 C's: Context 
Give Background!
content: Tells AI why you're asking & audience; Helps AI adopt right perspective
Good: "Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
Better: "Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
narration: Next up is Context. Why is background important?
It tells the AI why you're asking and who your audience is.
This helps the AI adopt the right perspective, doesn't it?
Adding context makes a good prompt even better, ensuring relevant results.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoonish illustration of an AI robot changing its glasses to different styles (e.g., 'student glasses', 'blogger glasses') to understand audience perspective.

slides.title:
The 3 C's: Constraints 
Set Rules!
content: Boundaries shape output; Specify length, format, style
Better: "Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."

Excellent: "Write a short blog post, under 400 words, for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city. Use a friendly and enthusiastic tone and end with a question to encourage comments."
narration: Finally, we have Constraints. What are these?
They are the rules you set for length, format, or style.
This clearly shapes the AI's output.
Adding constraints makes a better prompt excellent.
This gives you truly precise results. Makes sense, right?
slides.image_prompt: Cartoonish illustration of an AI robot carefully building a structure within clear boundary lines, using a ruler and blueprint.

slides.title: Bonus Tip: Persona
content: Tell the AI who to be
Example: "Act as an expert travel agent specializing in budget travel. Create a 5-day itinerary for a trip to Rome for a solo traveler who loves history and food."
narration: Bonus tip: Provide a Persona.
Tell the AI who to be!
Look at our example on screen: "Act as an expert travel agent..."
This helps the AI tailor its response perfectly, doesn't it?
slides.image_prompt: Cartoonish AI robot wearing different costumes (e.g., chef hat, doctor coat, travel agent attire) to represent different personas, interacting with a client.

slides.title: Giving Examples: Zero, One, Few-Shot
content: About giving AI examples to follow
Zero-Shot: no examples; One-Shot: one example; Few-Shot: a few examples
One-Shot Example: "Summarize text like this: Text: 'The sun is a star.' Output: 'Primary celestial body: Sun'. Now, use this format for the following text: [Insert Long Article Here]"
narration: Giving examples helps AI truly understand your needs. Have you tried this?
Zero-shot means no examples at all.
One-shot provides just one example.
Few-shot offers a few examples to learn from.
With one-shot, you show a pattern.
Like: 'Text: Sun is a star.' 'Output: Primary celestial body: Sun.'
slides.image_prompt: Cartoonish AI robot looking at a set of instructions: one showing no examples, one showing a single example, one showing multiple examples, illustrating pattern recognition.

slides.title: Advanced: Chain-of-Thought
content: For logic, math, reasoning; Add "think step-by-step" or "show your reasoning"
Reduces errors
Example: "I have 5 boxes of apples. Each box has 12 apples. I eat 3 apples and give away one full box. How many apples are left? Think step-by-step."
narration: For logic tasks, why not use Chain-of-Thought?
Simply add "think step-by-step" to your prompt.
This forces the AI to show its logic.
It significantly reduces errors. Isn't that clever?
slides.image_prompt: Cartoonish AI robot with thought bubbles showing step-by-step calculations or reasoning, illustrating a logical process.

slides.title: Advanced: Structuring Output
content: Tell AI how to organize information; Saves time
Example: "List the pros and cons of remote work. Provide the output as a Markdown table with two columns: 'Pros' and 'Cons'."
Formats: numbered list, HTML code, JSON, comma-separated list
narration: How can you make your AI output cleaner? Structure it!
Tell the AI exactly how to organize information, saving you valuable time.
You can ask for formats like Markdown tables, numbered lists, HTML, or JSON.
It's so versatile!
slides.image_prompt: A split screen showing unstructured text transforming into a neat markdown table, with icons for HTML, JSON, and list formats, cartoonish style.

slides.title: Advanced: Iterative Prompting
content: It's a conversation! First prompt rarely last
Refine prompts based on AI's output
Example: You: "Slogan for coffee shop." AI: "Brewing Happiness." You: "Shorter, modern." AI: "Urban Brews. Your Daily Grind." You: "Perfect!"
narration: Let's talk about Iterative Prompting. What is it? It's a conversation!
Your first prompt is rarely your last, is it?
You refine your requests based on the AI's output.
Think of it as a back-and-forth process.
You ask, AI responds, you refine, and the AI improves.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoonish depiction of a person and an AI robot having a back-and-forth conversation with speech bubbles showing refining ideas for a slogan.

slides.title: Practical Lab: Text Generation Challenge
content: Combine Persona, 3 C's, Structured Output

Prompt: "Act as a fitness coach. Create a simple 3-day workout plan for a beginner who wants to exercise at home with no equipment. The goal is a full-body workout. Present it in a table format with columns for 'Day', 'Exercise', and 'Duration'."
narration: Ready for a Text Generation Challenge?
Here, you'll combine a Persona, the 3 C's, and Structured Output.
Try using this prompt to create a fitness plan in a table format. Give it a go!
slides.image_prompt: Cartoonish fitness coach AI presenting a workout plan table to a beginner, with a friendly expression.

slides.title: Practical Lab: Image Prompting Challenge
content: Image tools use same principles; Focus on visual details, be descriptive
Prompt: "A close-up, photorealistic image of a cat wearing a tiny detective hat and magnifying glass, sitting in a library. The lighting is warm and cinematic."
narration: For Image Prompting, be descriptive! Can you paint a picture with words?
Always think like an artist.
Now for a challenge!
Imagine: "A close-up, photorealistic image of a cat."
This cat wears a tiny detective hat and magnifying glass.
It sits in a library.
The lighting is warm and cinematic.

slides.title: Assignment
content: Pick a topic: "Planning a weekend trip."
For an AI chatbot: 1. Write a vague prompt. 2. Improve it with Clarity, Context, and Constraints. 3. Add a Persona and ask for a structured output (e.g., numbered list or table).
Compare the outputs.
narration: Now for your assignment! Pick a topic, such as "planning a weekend trip."
First, write a vague prompt for an AI chatbot.
Then, improve it step-by-step using the 3 C's and adding a Persona.
Finally, ask for a structured output.
Then compare the results. See the difference?
